title: Hiring Household Help, Nannies & Drivers Legally in Türkiye
seoTitle: Hiring Household Help, Nannies & Drivers Legally in Türkiye
metaDescription: 2026 rules for hiring nannies and domestic staff legally in Türkiye: ÇSGB permits, SGK Ek-9, 102,503 TL fines, and Istanbul/Bodrum pay.
quickAnswer: Hiring domestic staff legally in Türkiye requires registering every Turkish or foreign worker with the Social Security Institution (SGK) under Article Ek-9, and securing a Ministry of Labor (ÇSGB) work permit before employing any foreign national. In 2026, employing an undocumented foreign worker carries a 102,503 TL fine per worker plus deportation costs.

body.text: Informal cash arrangements for nannies, housekeepers, and private drivers are common in expat circles, yet they expose foreign households to steep administrative fines, labor lawsuits, and residence permit complications. Understanding the exact boundary between Turkish-citizen hires and foreign-national permits keeps your household compliant from day one.

Independent of provider commissions."). We do not provide legal, employment, or payroll advice. Work permits and social security filings belong exclusively to the Ministry of Labor and Social Security (ÇSGB), SGK, and licensed Turkish labor attorneys or SMMMs.
What work permit and SGK social security rules apply to hiring domestic staff in Türkiye?

Households register Turkish citizens under [SGK Article Ek-9](https://www.sgk.gov.tr/Content/Post/2e0c9e1a-2cfe-4456-af10-49d3de0c58ba/Prime-Esas-Kazanc-Miktarlari-2026-01-14-10-35-39): under 10 days monthly requires daily accident cover, while 10+ days requires full monthly premiums. For foreign nationals, [ÇSGB rules](https://www.csgb.gov.tr/uigm/genel-bilgi/calisma-%C4%B1zni-degerlendirme-surecinde-gerekli-bilgi-ve-belgeler/) restrict domestic work permits strictly to childcare (under 15), eldercare (65+), or documented medical care.

You cannot legally obtain a domestic work permit for a foreign national solely as a general cleaner or private household driver without qualifying care grounds—drivers and general cleaners should be Turkish citizens (or hired through a licensed corporate transport/staffing firm). Applications for eligible foreign nannies are filed via the [ÇSGB e-İzin portal](https://ecalismaizni.csgb.gov.tr/) using the official [ÇSGB application guides](https://www.csgb.gov.tr/uigm/calisma-izni/basvuru-kilavuzlari/).

body.text: How do expat families vet English-speaking nannies safely?

Start by separating licensed placement agencies (registered with İŞKUR) from informal WhatsApp groups or unverified social media referrals. Before making an offer, verify the candidate's legal right to work in Türkiye, check at least two previous family references by phone, and request an official criminal record certificate (Adli Sicil Kaydı) via e-Devlet alongside a recent health screening.

body.text: What penalties apply for employing undocumented domestic workers?

Under [Law No. 6735's 2026 penalty schedule](http://www.ikanun.com/bilgi/6735-sayili-uluslararasi-isgucu-kanunu-idari-para-cezalari-2026-yili), employing an undocumented foreign worker incurs a 102,503 TL fine per worker for the employer. The dependent worker faces a 40,977 TL fine (82,010 TL if independent) plus possible deportation—with the employer liable for return-ticket, housing, and medical repatriation costs.
Failing to file mandatory SGK notifications triggers additional monthly social security fines and retroactive back-premiums with interest. Repeat offenses double the Law No. 6735 penalty.
What typical monthly salaries apply in Istanbul and Bodrum?

According to the [ÇSGB 2026 Wage Statistics Bulletin](https://csgb.gov.tr/yayinlar/calisma-hayati-istatistikleri-e-bulteni/ekim-2026/ucret-ve-sendikal-istatistikler.html), Türkiye's 2026 statutory minimum wage is 28,075.50 TL net (33,030.00 TL gross, with an undiscounted employer cost of 40,874.63 TL). In practice, experienced bilingual or English-speaking nannies and full-time household drivers in Istanbul and Bodrum command well above the statutory floor.

In Istanbul (Beşiktaş, Sarıyer, Kadıköy, Şişli), expect roughly 45,000–75,000 TL+ net per month for an experienced English-speaking live-out or live-in nanny, and 40,000–60,000 TL+ net for a full-time private driver, plus SGK premiums and meal/transport allowances. In Bodrum, summer-season demand (May–October) often pushes live-in nanny and driver rates 15%–25% higher than off-season winter rates, and housing must usually be factored in.

faq.q: Can a foreign resident with an Ikamet sponsor a foreign nanny's work permit?
faq.a: Yes, provided the sponsoring expat household meets ÇSGB's qualifying care criteria (such as a child under 15 or an elderly/medical care need), demonstrates sufficient regular income, and applies through the e-İzin system with an active electronic signature.

faq.q: Can I hire a foreign nanny who only holds a tourist residence permit (Ikamet)?
faq.a: Not until her work permit is officially approved. Holding a tourist or short-term Ikamet does not grant work authorization; employing her before ÇSGB approval still triggers the 102,503 TL undocumented-worker fine in 2026.

faq.q: What is the difference between SGK Ek-9 under 10 days and 10+ days?
faq.a: Under SGK Article Ek-9, domestic workers hired for fewer than 10 days a month only require a low daily occupational accident/disease premium, whereas workers employed 10 or more days a month require full monthly social security, health, and pension contributions.

faq.q: Should I pay my nanny or driver in cash or by bank transfer?
faq.a: Always pay via bank transfer into the employee's own Turkish IBAN with a clear payment reference (such as "Maaş / Salary"). Bank records protect both employer and employee in the event of an SGK inspection or severance dispute.

faq.q: Do domestic workers in Türkiye accrue severance pay (Kıdem Tazminatı)?
faq.a: Yes. Under Turkish labor practice, full-time domestic workers employed continuously for one year or more can accrue statutory leave and termination/severance entitlements—consult a Turkish labor lawyer or SMMM before drafting or ending a contract.

faq.q: How long does a foreign domestic work permit take to approve in 2026?
faq.a: Standard ÇSGB e-İzin processing typically takes 30 to 60 days once all employer income documents, care-eligibility proofs, and employee filings are submitted cleanly, though incomplete files add weeks of delay.
